Synthetic tester requirement: transfer order
This is maintenance evaluation data, not a real company requirement.

Existing business: an order belongs to an origin warehouse. Its states are Draft,
Ready, InTransit, Completed. Each parcel belongs to one order. The origin warehouse
shows its reserved quantity; the destination shows incoming quantity. These are
visible UI values. Existing binding and quantities can be checked by order ID.

This feature creates a transfer for a Ready order. A transfer accepts 1 through 20
parcels, inclusive, in whole parcels. Empty selection is rejected. Each selected
parcel must have a nonempty tracking number and belong to the selected order.
The destination warehouse must differ from the origin.

For orders in Ready, creation is allowed only when both payment is confirmed and
stock is allocated. These are independent yes/no business conditions: all four
combinations can be prepared using the test data described below. For each other
combination the operation is rejected without changing the order or warehouse
quantities. Do not invent exact error wording; the reason must identify the
violated business condition.

Roles: origin warehouse operator may create transfers for their own warehouse;
another warehouse operator may view the order but cannot create its transfer;
viewer may view but cannot create a transfer. All three roles can view the incoming
quantity. Ownership scope is enforced even if an order is found by ID.

State events: create-transfer and finish-transfer. In Draft neither is allowed.
In Ready, create-transfer may move the order to InTransit subject to the other
rules; finish-transfer is rejected. In InTransit, repeated create-transfer is
rejected without another transfer or incoming increment; finish-transfer moves
the order to Completed. In Completed both events are rejected, preserving state.

On successful creation, selected parcel bindings remain on that order, the order
becomes InTransit, origin reserved quantity remains unchanged, and destination
incoming quantity increases by exactly the selected parcel count. On completion,
destination incoming decreases by the transferred count; parcel bindings remain
unchanged. Rejection for any invalid selection, permission, payment/stock or state
must preserve the existing order state, parcel bindings, and both quantities.

All preparation/reset is performed through a supplied tester-visible data console
on a dedicated test environment. It can create named synthetic orders with chosen
states, independent payment/stock flags, parcels including missing tracking and
wrong-order records, and baseline quantities. It supports each role and warehouse
scope and restores the named records. No product code is available at design time.
This console is context for reproducibility, not evidence the implementation works.
Target: one business client called qa-client; its UI control tool is available in
the eventual test environment. Build/address/account session are runtime inputs.

Scope: test design only. Do not add API/unit tests, unspecified performance limits,
exact error text, notification rules, or unsupported platform variants.
